items.title: 8.3.1 Application of the Binomial Theorem (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 158-161: 8.3.1 Application of the Binomial Theorem: Approximations, Summation of infinite series, Examples 16-20 (Example 16 with its alternative method)

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein humne dekha ke negative ya fractional power wali binomial series kabhi khatam nahin hoti. Ab sawal yeh hai ke is lambi series ka faida kya? Is sabaq mein do bare faide dekhenge: (1) approximations, yani mushkil roots aur powers (jaise \(\sqrt[3]{30}\)) ki qeemat sirf teen chaar terms se nikaalna; aur (2) infinite series ka jor (sum) nikaalna. Dono kaam Board exams mein aksar aate hain.

Approximations: \((1 + x)^{n}\) ke particular cases mein humne dekha ke har agli term mein \(x\) ki power barhti jati hai. Kyun ke \(|x| < 1\), is liye
\[|x|^{r} < |x| \quad \text{for } r = 2, 3, 4, \dots\]
Yeh baat batati hai ke agar \(|x| < 1\) ho to har expansion ki terms number ke lihaz se (numerically) chhoti hoti jati hain. Is liye negative integer ya fraction index wali expansions ki taqreebi (approximate) qeemat ke liye binomial series ki shuru ki chand terms kaafi hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Chand terms kaafi kyun hain? \(x = 0.1\) ho to \(x^{2} = 0.01\), \(x^{3} = 0.001\), \(x^{4} = 0.0001\): har power pichli se das guna chhoti. Teen chaar terms ke baad baqi terms sirf chauthe paanchve decimal ko chhooti hain. Is liye "teen decimal tak sahi" jawab ke liye terms tab tak lijiye jab tak woh taqreeban 0.0005 se chhoti na ho jayein.
Kisi number ka root ya power nikaalne ka nuskha: number ko (aasan number) \(\times\) (\(1 \pm\) chhota number) likhiye, aasan number ko bracket se bahar nikaaliye, phir expand kijiye. Misal: \(30 = 27\left(1 + \frac{1}{9}\right)\), \(0.8 = 1 - 0.2\), \(99 = 100\left(1 - \frac{1}{100}\right)\). Example 16 aur 17 yahi dikhate hain.
Hamari taraf se misaal: rozmarra mein bhi hum yahi karte hain. \(1.01^{10}\) (1% munafa das saal) ka andaza: \(1 + 10(0.01) + 45(0.0001) = 1.1045\), aur asal qeemat \(1.10462\dots\).

Summation of infinite series: Binomial series infinite series ka jor nikaalne mein bohat kaam aati hai. Jis series ka jor chahiye use
\[1 + nx + \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{2}\]
\[+ \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3!}x^{3} + \dots\]
se milaate (compare karte) hain taa ke \(n\) aur \(x\) ki values mil jayein. Phir \(n\) aur \(x\) ki values \((1 + x)^{n}\) mein rakh kar jor nikaal lete hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh theorem ka ulta istemal hai: \((1 + x)^{n}\) ko kholne ke bajaye, humein khuli hui series di jati hai aur pehchaanna hota hai ke yeh kis \((1 + x)^{n}\) se bani. Doosri term ko \(nx\) ke barabar aur teesri term ko \(\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{2}\) ke barabar rakhne se do equations milti hain, jin se \(n\) aur \(x\) nikal aate hain. Bilkul jaise kisi ka chehra dekh kar pehchaan lena ke yeh kis ka beta hai! Example 20 yahi karta hai.
Ab kitab ki paanch misaalein ek ek kar ke hal karte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Approximation wale har sawal ka ek hi dhaancha hai; ise yaad kar lijiye:
1. Number ko \((1 + x)^{n}\) ki shakal mein laaiye, jahan \(x\) chhota ho (aksar aasan number bahar nikaal kar).
2. Shart likhiye: \(|x| < 1\).
3. Teen chaar terms tak expand kijiye.
4. Har term ko decimal mein badal kar jama kijiye, aur dekhiye ke agli term itni chhoti hai ke maangi gayi decimal jagah ko nahin chhooti.
5. Maange gaye decimal tak round kijiye.
Example 16 mein pehle algebraic expansion milti hai aur phir usi mein \(x = .1\) rakha jata hai; Example 17 mein seedha number ka cube root nikaala jata hai. Dono mein yahi paanch qadam hain.

blocks.title: Example 16
blocks.problem: Expand \((1 - 2x)^{1/3}\) to four terms and apply it to evaluate \((.8)^{1/3}\) correct to three places of decimal.
steps:
Given: \((1 - 2x)^{1/3}\); yani \(n = \frac{1}{3}\), aur formula wale "\(x\)" ki jagah \(-2x\) hai.
To find: (1) pehli chaar terms; (2) \((.8)^{1/3}\) teen decimal tak.
Method: fractional index ki binomial series. Doosre hisse ke liye dekhiye ke \(1 - 2x = .8\) tab hota hai jab \(x = .1\); is liye chaar terms mein \(x = .1\) rakh denge. Yani ek hi expansion se do kaam.

Step 1: Shart (condition of validity)
Yeh expansion sirf tab sahi hai jab \(|2x| < 1\) ya \(2|x| < 1\) ya \(|x| < \frac{1}{2}\).
Kyun: binomial series ke liye bracket ki doosri term ki absolute value 1 se kam honi chahiye; yahan doosri term \(-2x\) hai, sirf \(x\) nahin. Yeh shart likhna exam mein zaroori hai.

Step 2: Pehli chaar terms likhein
\[(1 - 2x)^{1/3} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{3}(-2x)\]
\[+ \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{3} - 1\right)}{2!}(-2x)^{2}\]
\[+ \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{3} - 1\right)\left(\frac{1}{3} - 2\right)}{3!}(-2x)^{3} + \dots\]
Kyun: yeh \(1 + nx + \frac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{2} + \frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3!}x^{3}\) hai jis mein \(n = \frac{1}{3}\) aur \(x\) ki jagah \(-2x\) rakha gaya. Dhyan dein: \(-2x\) ko bracket mein rakhiye, warna power lagate waqt minus ya 2 chhoot jata hai.

Step 3: Simplify karein
\[= 1 - \dfrac{2}{3}x\]
\[+ \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)}{2 \cdot 1}(4x^{2})\]
\[+ \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)}{3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1}(-8x^{3}) + \dots\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{2}{3}x - \dfrac{4}{9}x^{2}\]
\[- \dfrac{1 \cdot 2 \cdot 5}{3 \cdot 3 \cdot 3}\cdot\dfrac{1}{3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1}(8x^{3}) - \dots\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{2}{3}x - \dfrac{4}{9}x^{2} - \dfrac{40}{81}x^{3} - \dots\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{3} - 1 = -\frac{2}{3}\), \(\frac{1}{3} - 2 = -\frac{5}{3}\); \((-2x)^{2} = 4x^{2}\), \((-2x)^{3} = -8x^{3}\). Teesri term: \(\frac{-2/9}{2}\cdot 4 = -\frac{4}{9}\). Chauthi term: \(\frac{10/27}{6}\cdot(-8) = -\frac{80}{162} = -\frac{40}{81}\). Signs dhyan se: do negative factors milkar positive, phir \(-8\) se negative.

Step 4: \(x = .1\) rakhein
Upar wali expansion mein \(x = .1\) rakhne se
\[(1 - 2(.1))^{1/3}\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{2}{3}(.1) - \dfrac{4}{9}(.1)^{2}\]
\[- \dfrac{40}{81}(.1)^{3} - \dots\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{.2}{3} - \dfrac{.04}{9} - \dfrac{.04}{81} - \dots\]
\[\approx 1 - .06666 - .00444 - .00049\]
\[= 1 - .07159 = .92841\]
Kyun: \(1 - 2(.1) = .8\), yani wahi number jis ka cube root chahiye; aur \(x = .1\) shart \(|x| < \frac{1}{2}\) poori karta hai. \(40 \times .001 = .04\).

Step 5: Round karein
Lihaza \((.8)^{1/3} \approx .928\)
Kyun: agli term \(-\frac{160}{243}x^{4}\) hai, jo \(x = .1\) par taqreeban \(-0.00007\) banti hai; yeh teesre decimal ko nahin badal sakti, is liye .928 pakka hai.

Alternative method (kitab yeh aap par chhorti hai; yahan poora hal kiya gaya hai)
\[(.8)^{1/3} = (1 - .2)^{1/3}\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{.2}{3}\]
\[+ \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{3} - 1\right)}{2!}(-.2)^{2}\]
\[+ \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{3} - 1\right)\left(\frac{1}{3} - 2\right)}{3!}(-.2)^{3} + \dots\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{.2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{9}(.04)\]
\[- \dfrac{5}{81}(.008) - \dots\]
\[\approx 1 - .06667 - .00444 - .00049\]
\[= .92840 \approx .928\]
Kyun: yahan hum seedha \((1 - .2)^{1/3}\) ko \(n = \frac{1}{3}\) aur \(x = -.2\) ke saath kholte hain. Coefficients wahi \(\frac{1}{3}\), \(-\frac{1}{9}\), \(\frac{5}{81}\) hain; \((-.2)^{2} = .04\), \((-.2)^{3} = -.008\). Dono tareeqon se ek hi jawab aaya.

Tasdeeq:
\(.928^{3} = .7992\dots\), jo .8 ke bohat qareeb hai. Calculator se \((.8)^{1/3} = .92832\dots\), yani teen decimal tak .928.

blocks.text:
Example 16 se kya seekha? Ek dafa \((1 - 2x)^{1/3}\) ki general expansion mil jaye to us mein \(x\) ki koi bhi chhoti value rakh kar mukhtalif numbers ke cube roots nikaal sakte hain: \(x = .05\) se \((.9)^{1/3}\), \(x = .1\) se \((.8)^{1/3}\). Lekin \(x = .6\) nahin rakh sakte, kyun ke shart \(|x| < \frac{1}{2}\) toot jati hai. Isi liye shart sab se pehle likhi jati hai.
Hamari taraf se misaal: \(\frac{1}{1.02} = (1 + 0.02)^{-1} \approx 1 - 0.02 + 0.0004 = 0.9804\). Calculator: \(0.980392\dots\). Do decimal mein bilkul wahi, aur chaar decimal tak bhi sahi.

Example 17 mein sab se ahem faisla yeh hai ke 30 ko kis perfect cube ke saath likhein. Sochiye agar 8 lete: \(30 = 8\left(1 + \frac{22}{8}\right)\), yani \(x = 2.75\), jo 1 se bara hai; series chalegi hi nahin. Agar 64 lete: \(30 = 64\left(1 - \frac{34}{64}\right)\), \(x \approx -0.53\); shart to poori hai magar terms bohat aahista chhoti hoti hain aur bohat si terms leni parti hain. 27 lene se \(x = \frac{1}{9} \approx 0.11\), jo kaafi chhota hai, aur teen terms mein kaam ho jata hai. Usool: hamesha sab se qareeb perfect power chuniye, taa ke \(x\) jitna ho sake chhota ho.

blocks.title: Example 17
blocks.problem: Evaluate \(\sqrt[3]{30}\) correct to three places of decimal.
steps:
Given: \(\sqrt[3]{30} = (30)^{1/3}\).
To find: is ki qeemat teen decimal tak.
Method: 30 ke sab se qareeb perfect cube 27 hai (\(3^{3}\)). Is liye \(30 = 27 + 3 = 27\left(1 + \frac{1}{9}\right)\) likhenge, \(27^{1/3} = 3\) bahar nikaalenge, aur \(\left(1 + \frac{1}{9}\right)^{1/3}\) ko expand karenge, jahan \(x = \frac{1}{9}\) chhota hai.

Step 1: Perfect cube bahar nikaalein
\[\sqrt[3]{30} = (30)^{1/3} = (27 + 3)^{1/3}\]
\[= \left[27\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{27}\right)\right]^{1/3}\]
\[= (27)^{1/3}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{9}\right)^{1/3}\]
\[= 3\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{9}\right)^{1/3}\]
Kyun: binomial series ko \((1 + x)^{n}\) ki shakal aur chhota \(x\) chahiye. \((27 + 3)^{1/3}\) ko seedha nahin khol sakte kyun ke bracket 1 se shuru nahin hota; 27 bahar nikaalne se \(\frac{3}{27} = \frac{1}{9}\) bacha jo chhota hai.

Step 2: Expand karein
\[= 3\left[1 + \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{1}{9}\right.\]
\[+ \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)}{2!}\left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right)^{2}\]
\[\left. + \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)}{3!}\left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right)^{3} + \dots\right]\]
\[= 3\left[1 + \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{1}{9} - \dfrac{1}{9}\left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right)^{2}\right.\]
\[\left. + \dfrac{5}{81}\left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right)^{3} + \dots\right]\]
\[= 3\left[1 + \dfrac{1}{27} - \left(\dfrac{1}{27}\right)^{2} + \dots\right]\]
Kyun: \(n = \frac{1}{3}\) ke saath: \(nx = \frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{9}\); \(\frac{n(n-1)}{2!} = \frac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)}{2} = -\frac{1}{9}\); \(\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3!} = \frac{5}{81}\). Aur \(\frac{1}{9}\cdot\frac{1}{81} = \frac{1}{729} = \left(\frac{1}{27}\right)^{2}\).

Step 3: Decimals mein badlein
\[\approx 3[1 + .03704 - .001372]\]
\[= 3[1.035668] = 3.107004\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{27} = .037037\dots \approx .03704\) aur \(\frac{1}{729} \approx .001372\). Chauthi term \(3 \cdot \frac{5}{81}\cdot\frac{1}{729} \approx .00025\) teesre decimal ko nahin badalti, is liye teen terms kaafi hain.

Step 4: Round karein
Lihaza \(\sqrt[3]{30} \approx 3.107\)
Kyun: sawal teen decimal maangta hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(3.107^{3} = 29.993\dots\), jo 30 ke bohat qareeb hai; calculator se \(\sqrt[3]{30} = 3.10723\dots\).

blocks.text: Examples 16 aur 17 ke baad ek zaroori sawal: jawab ko kaise check karein jab calculator na ho? Do aasan tareeqe hain. Pehla: jawab ko ulta chala kar dekhiye. \(\sqrt[3]{30} \approx 3.107\) hai to \(3.107 \times 3.107 \times 3.107\) taqreeban 30 aana chahiye; aata hai (29.993). Doosra: agli term ka andaza lagaiye. Agar agli term maangi gayi decimal jagah se kaafi chhoti hai to jawab pakka hai. Misal: teen decimal ke liye agli term 0.0005 se chhoti honi chahiye; Example 17 mein woh taqreeban 0.00025 hai, is liye 3.107 bilkul theek hai. Yeh aadat exam hall mein aap ko ghalat rounding se bachayegi, aur aap ko apne jawab par bharosa bhi degi.

Ab Example 18 ek naye qisam ka sawal hai: do cheezon ke product mein kisi khaas power ka coefficient. Yahan poori expansion likhna mumkin hi nahin kyun ke terms be-shumar hain. Tareeqa yeh hai ke soch kar dekhein ke \(x^{n}\) kin kin jor se banta hai. \((1 - x)\) ki sirf do terms hain, \(1\) aur \(-x\). \(1\) ko \(x^{n}\) wali term chahiye, aur \(-x\) ko \(x^{n-1}\) wali term chahiye taa ke product mein \(x^{n}\) aaye. Bas yahi do contributions jama karne hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Isi tareeqe ki ek aasan misaal: \(\frac{1 + x}{1 - x}\) mein \(x^{3}\) ka coefficient.
\[\dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x} = (1 + x)(1 - x)^{-1}\]
\[= (1 + x)(1 + x + x^{2} + x^{3} + \dots)\]
\(x^{3}\) do jagah se: \(1 \times x^{3}\) aur \(x \times x^{2}\). Coefficient \(1 + 1 = 2\). Check: \(x = 0.1\) par \(\frac{1.1}{0.9} = 1.2222\dots\) aur \(1 + 2(0.1) + 2(0.01) + 2(0.001) + \dots = 1.2222\dots\) Wah!

blocks.title: Example 18
blocks.problem: Find the coefficient of \(x^{n}\) in the expansion of \(\frac{1-x}{(1+x)^{2}}\).
steps:
Given: \(\frac{1 - x}{(1 + x)^{2}}\) (hum \(|x| < 1\) maante hain).
To find: \(x^{n}\) ka coefficient.
Method: ise \((1 - x)(1 + x)^{-2}\) likhenge. \((1 + x)^{-2}\) ki general term case (ii) se \((-1)^{r}(r + 1)x^{r}\) hai. Product mein \(x^{n}\) do jagah se banta hai: \(1 \times\) (\(x^{n}\) wali term) aur \(-x \times\) (\(x^{n-1}\) wali term). Bas yeh do hisse jorne hain.

Step 1: Product ki shakal
\[\dfrac{1 - x}{(1 + x)^{2}} = (1 - x)(1 + x)^{-2}\]
Kyun: \((1 + x)^{2}\) se divide karna \((1 + x)^{-2}\) se multiply karne ke barabar hai, aur negative power wali cheez hum expand kar sakte hain.

Step 3: \(x^{n-1}\) aur \(x^{n}\) wali terms dikhayein
\[= (1 - x)[1 + (-1)2x + (-1)^{2}3x^{2} + \dots\]
\[+ (-1)^{n-1}nx^{n-1} + (-1)^{n}(n + 1)x^{n} + \dots]\]
Kyun: \((-1)^{r}(r + 1)x^{r}\) mein \(r = n - 1\) aur \(r = n\) rakhne se yeh do terms milti hain. Sirf yahi do humare kaam ki hain.

Step 4: \(x^{n}\) ka coefficient jama karein
\[\text{Coefficient of } x^{n}\]
\[= (-1)(-1)^{n-1}n + (-1)^{n}(n + 1)\]
\[= (-1)^{n}n + (-1)^{n}(n + 1)\]
\[= (-1)^{n}[n + (n + 1)]\]
\[= (-1)^{n}(2n + 1)\]
Kyun: \(1 \times (-1)^{n}(n + 1)x^{n}\), aur \((-x)\times(-1)^{n-1}nx^{n-1} = (-1)^{n}nx^{n}\), kyun ke \((-1)(-1)^{n-1} = (-1)^{n}\). Phir \((-1)^{n}\) common.
Dhyan dein: \(-x\) wala hissa bhool jana sab se aam ghalti hai; tab jawab sirf \((-1)^{n}(n + 1)\) aata hai jo ghalat hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 18 mein kitab ki pehli expansion line "\([1 + -2x + (-2)x + \dots\)" chhapti hai, yani \(x\) wali term do dafa likhi gayi. Sahi bracket \([1 + (-2)x + \frac{(-2)(-3)}{2!}x^{2} + \dots]\) hai. Agli do lines mein \((-1)\), \((-1)^{2}\), \((-1)^{r}\) aur \((-x + 1)\) ke minus signs chhape hi nahin. Kitab ka final jawab \((-1)^{n}(2n + 1)\) sahi hai; upar humne har line sahi likhi hai.

Example 19 mein jumla aata hai "\(x\) itna chhota hai ke us ka cube aur oonchi powers neglect ki ja sakti hain". Is ka matlab samajh lijiye: agar \(x = 0.01\) ho to \(x^{2} = 0.0001\) aur \(x^{3} = 0.000001\). \(x^{3}\) itna chhota hai ke jawab par us ka asar na hone ke barabar hai. Is liye hum har bracket ko sirf \(x^{2}\) tak kholte hain, aur multiply karte waqt bhi \(x^{3}\) ya oopar wale products ko seedha chhor dete hain. Is se kaam bohat chhota ho jata hai. Yaad rahe, "\(\approx\)" (taqreeban barabar) ka nishan isi wajah se lagta hai, "\(=\)" ka nahin.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Examples 18 aur 19 dono mein do brackets ka product hai, lekin farq samajh lijiye: Example 18 mein ek bracket \((1 - x)\) chhota sa hai aur doosra infinite, aur humein kisi bhi \(n\) ke liye coefficient chahiye. Example 19 mein dono brackets infinite hain, lekin sirf \(x^{2}\) tak kaam hai. Dono jagah asool ek hai: socho ke maangi gayi power kin kin terms ke milne se banti hai, aur sirf unhi ko multiply karo. Baqi sab terms ko likhne ki zaroorat hi nahin.

blocks.title: Example 19
blocks.problem: If \(x\) is so small that its cube and higher power can be neglected, show that \(\sqrt{\frac{1-x}{1+x}} \approx 1 - x + \frac{1}{2}x^{2}\).
steps:
Given: \(\sqrt{\frac{1-x}{1+x}}\); \(x^{3}\) aur us se oonchi powers chhor sakte hain.
To show: yeh taqreeban \(1 - x + \frac{1}{2}x^{2}\) hai.
Method: root ko \((1 - x)^{1/2}(1 + x)^{-1/2}\) likhenge, har bracket ko \(x^{2}\) tak kholenge, multiply karenge, aur sirf \(x^{2}\) tak ki terms rakhenge. "Cube neglect" ka matlab hai ke \(x^{3}\) itna chhota hai ke use zero samjha ja sakta hai.

Step 1: Powers ki shakal mein likhein
\[\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}} = (1 - x)^{1/2}(1 + x)^{-1/2}\]
Kyun: square root \(\frac{1}{2}\) power hai, aur \((1 + x)^{1/2}\) se divide karna \((1 + x)^{-1/2}\) se multiply karna hai. Ab do brackets hain jinhein alag alag khol sakte hain.

Step 2: Har bracket \(x^{2}\) tak kholein
\[(1 - x)^{1/2} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}(-x)\]
\[+ \dfrac{\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2} - 1\right)}{2!}(-x)^{2} + \dots\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x - \dfrac{1}{8}x^{2} + \dots\]
\[(1 + x)^{-1/2} = 1 + \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)x\]
\[+ \dfrac{\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{1}{2} - 1\right)}{2!}x^{2} + \dots\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{3}{8}x^{2} + \dots\]
Kyun: \(\frac{\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)}{2} = -\frac{1}{8}\) aur \(\frac{\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}{2} = \frac{3}{8}\). \(x^{3}\) wali terms ki zaroorat nahin kyun ke sawal unhein chhorne ko kehta hai.

Step 3: Multiply karein aur \(x^{2}\) tak rakhein
\[\left[1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x - \dfrac{1}{8}x^{2} + \dots\right]\]
\[\times\left[1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{3}{8}x^{2} + \dots\right]\]
\[= \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{3}{8}x^{2}\right)\]
\[+ \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{1}{4}x^{2}\right) - \dfrac{1}{8}x^{2} + \dots\]
\[= 1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)x\]
\[+ \left(\dfrac{3}{8} + \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{8}\right)x^{2} + \dots\]
\[\approx 1 - x + \dfrac{1}{2}x^{2}\]
Kyun: pehle bracket ki teen terms \(1\), \(-\frac{1}{2}x\), \(-\frac{1}{8}x^{2}\) har ek doosre bracket se multiply hoti hain; jo product \(x^{3}\) ya oopar deta hai use chhor dete hain. Phir \(\frac{3}{8} + \frac{2}{8} - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\).
Dhyan dein: \(x^{2}\) teen jagah se banta hai (\(1 \cdot \frac{3}{8}x^{2}\), \(-\frac{1}{2}x \cdot -\frac{1}{2}x\), \(-\frac{1}{8}x^{2}\cdot 1\)); koi ek bhi chhoota to jawab ghalat.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 19 mein final result ke baad kitab ek faltu line "\(= \sqrt{3}\)" chhapti hai. Is misaal mein kahin \(\sqrt{3}\) nahin; yeh line misprint hai aur ise nazar andaaz kijiye. Sahi natija \(\sqrt{\frac{1-x}{1+x}} \approx 1 - x + \frac{1}{2}x^{2}\) hi hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Series ka jor pehchaanne ki ek aasan misaal pehle dekh lein: \(1 + 2\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) + 3\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{2} + 4\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{3} + \dots\) ka jor kya hai?
Coefficients 1, 2, 3, 4, ... dekh kar case (v) yaad aata hai: \((1 - x)^{-2} = 1 + 2x + 3x^{2} + \dots\). Yahan \(x = \frac{1}{3}\), jo \(|x| < 1\) hai. Is liye jor
\[\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{-2} = \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{-2} = \dfrac{9}{4}\]
Example 20 mein series itni seedhi pehchaan mein nahin aati, is liye wahan \(n\) aur \(x\) ko equations bana kar nikaalte hain. Lekin idea wahi hai: di hui series ko kisi \((1 + x)^{n}\) ka chehra pehnaana.

blocks.title: Example 20
steps:
Given: infinite series \(y\).
To show: \(5y^{2} + 10y - 4 = 0\).
Method: yeh "summation of infinite series" ka sawal hai. Series ke shuru mein 1 nahin, is liye dono taraf 1 jama karenge. Phir use \(1 + nx + \frac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{2} + \dots\) se compare kar ke \(n\) aur \(x\) nikaalenge; tab \(1 + y = (1 + x)^{n}\). Aakhir mein square kar ke root khatam karenge.

Step 1: Series likhein aur 1 jama karein
\[y = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right) + \dfrac{1 \cdot 3}{4 \cdot 2!}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right)^{2}\]
\[+ \dfrac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{8 \cdot 3!}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right)^{3} + \dots \quad \text{(A)}\]
\[1 + y = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right)\]
\[+ \dfrac{1 \cdot 3}{4 \cdot 2!}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right)^{2}\]
\[+ \dfrac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{8 \cdot 3!}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right)^{3} + \dots \quad \text{(B)}\]
Kyun: binomial series hamesha 1 se shuru hoti hai; 1 jama karne se (B) us shakal mein aa gayi. \(2^{2} = 4\) aur \(2^{3} = 8\).

Step 2: Binomial series se milaayein
Maan lijiye (B) ke right side wali series is ke barabar (identical) hai:
\[1 + nx + \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{2}\]
\[+ \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3!}x^{3} + \dots\]
jo \((1 + x)^{n}\) ki expansion hai, jab \(|x| < 1\) aur \(n\) positive integer na ho.
Kyun: agar do series bilkul ek jaisi hain to un ki doosri terms aapas mein barabar aur teesri terms aapas mein barabar hongi.

Step 3: Do equations
Dono series ki terms milaane se
\[nx = \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right) \quad \text{(i)}\]
\[\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{2} = \dfrac{1 \cdot 3}{4 \cdot 2!}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right)^{2} \quad \text{(ii)}\]
\[\text{From (i): } x = \dfrac{2}{9n} \quad \text{(iii)}\]
Kyun: (i) doosri terms ko aur (ii) teesri terms ko barabar rakhta hai. (i) se \(nx = \frac{2}{9}\), is liye \(x = \frac{2}{9n}\).

Step 4: \(n\) nikaalein
(ii) mein \(x = \frac{2}{9n}\) rakhne se
\[\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}\cdot\left(\dfrac{2}{9n}\right)^{2} = \dfrac{3}{8}\cdot\dfrac{16}{81}\]
\[\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}\cdot\dfrac{4}{81n^{2}} = \dfrac{3}{8}\cdot\dfrac{16}{81}\]
\[\dfrac{2(n-1)}{81n} = \dfrac{6}{81}\]
\[2(n - 1) = 6n\]
\[n - 1 = 3n \Rightarrow n = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1 \cdot 3}{4 \cdot 2!} = \frac{3}{8}\) aur \(\frac{3}{8}\cdot\frac{16}{81} = \frac{6}{81}\). Left side par \(n^{2}\) mein se ek \(n\) kat jata hai. Dono taraf \(\frac{81n}{2}\) se multiply karne par \(n - 1 = 3n\).

Step 5: \(x\) nikaalein
(iii) mein \(n = -\frac{1}{2}\) rakhne se
\[x = \dfrac{2}{9\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)} = -\dfrac{4}{9}\]
Kyun: \(9 \times \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{9}{2}\), aur \(2 \div \left(-\frac{9}{2}\right) = -\frac{4}{9}\). Ghor kijiye \(|x| = \frac{4}{9} < 1\), is liye series sahi (valid) hai.

Step 6: Series ka jor
\[1 + y = \left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right)^{-1/2} = \left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right)^{-1/2}\]
\[= \left(\dfrac{9}{5}\right)^{1/2} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{5}}\]
\[\sqrt{5}(1 + y) = 3 \quad \text{(iv)}\]
Kyun: \(1 + y = (1 + x)^{n}\), jahan \(x = -\frac{4}{9}\), \(n = -\frac{1}{2}\). Negative power fraction ko ulat deti hai: \(\left(\frac{5}{9}\right)^{-1/2} = \left(\frac{9}{5}\right)^{1/2} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}\).

Step 7: (iv) ki dono sides ka square
\[5(1 + 2y + y^{2}) = 9\]
\[5 + 10y + 5y^{2} = 9\]
\[5y^{2} + 10y - 4 = 0\]
Kyun: square karne se \(\sqrt{5}\) khatam: \(5(1 + y)^{2} = 9\). Phir \((1 + y)^{2}\) khol kar 9 ko left le aaye.

Tasdeeq:
\(n = -\frac{1}{2}\), \(x = -\frac{4}{9}\) se chauthi term \(\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3!}x^{3} = \frac{20}{729}\) aati hai, aur sawal ki chauthi term \(\frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{8 \cdot 6}\cdot\frac{64}{729} = \frac{20}{729}\) hai: dono barabar. Aur \(y = \frac{3}{\sqrt{5}} - 1 \approx 0.3416\) rakhne par \(5y^{2} + 10y - 4 = 0.5836 + 3.4164 - 4 = 0\).
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(1 + y = \frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}\), is liye \(5y^{2} + 10y - 4 = 0\).

blocks.text: Example 20 ka khulasa: humne kabhi infinite terms jama nahin kin. Sirf doosri aur teesri term se \(n = -\frac{1}{2}\) aur \(x = -\frac{4}{9}\) pehchaane, aur baqi kaam formula ne kar diya. Exam mein aisa sawal aaye to (A), (B), (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) jaise labels zaroor lagaiye, taa ke examiner aap ki soch ka raasta asaani se dekh sake. Aur aakhir mein \(|x| < 1\) check karna na bhooliye; agar \(x\) ki value 1 se bari aaye to series ka jor is formula se nahin nikaala ja sakta.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(\sqrt{99}\) ko binomial se kaise nikaalenge? (Ishara: \(99 = 100\left(1 - \frac{1}{100}\right)\), to \(\sqrt{99} = 10\left(1 - \frac{1}{100}\right)^{1/2} \approx 10(1 - 0.005 - 0.0000125) = 9.94987\).) Yeh Exercise 8.3 ka sawal 2(i) bhi hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(|x| < 1\) par binomial series ki terms chhoti hoti jati hain, is liye chand terms se achha andaza mil jata hai.
2. Kisi number ka root nikaalna ho to sab se qareeb perfect power bahar nikaaliye: \(\sqrt[3]{30} = 3\left(1 + \frac{1}{9}\right)^{1/3}\).
3. Validity ki shart (jaise \(|2x| < 1\)) hamesha likhiye.
4. Product \((1 - x)(1 + x)^{-2}\) mein \(x^{n}\) ka coefficient: har hisse se \(x^{n}\) wali term jama kijiye.
5. Series ka jor: pehle 1 se shuru karaiye, 2nd aur 3rd term ko \(nx\) aur \(\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{2}\) se milaaiye, phir jor \((1 + x)^{n}\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \((27 + 3)^{1/3}\) ko seedha kholna: bracket 1 se shuru hona chahiye, pehle 27 bahar nikaaliye.
2. \((-2x)^{3} = -8x^{3}\) bhool jana (odd power par minus rehta hai).
3. Example 19 jaise products mein \(x^{3}\) terms rakh lena jinhein chhorna tha, ya \(x^{2}\) ka koi product chhor dena.
4. Example 20 mein compare karne se pehle dono taraf 1 jama karna bhool jana.
